title: Mushroom Rigatoni
subtitle: Rigatoni with chestnut mushrooms in a creamy white wine sauce
excerpt: Chestnut mushrooms cooked down in white wine with garlic and a little cream, tossed through rigatoni. Rich, earthy, and ready in half an hour.
sourceNotes: Italian-inspired weeknight pasta; dried porcini in the sauce add depth without much extra effort.

content.text: This is a simple mushroom pasta that gets its depth from cooking the mushrooms in two stages: first on high heat to drive off water and build colour, then low and slow in wine and cream. Do not crowd the pan or the mushrooms will steam rather than brown.

items.prepNote: soaked in 100ml boiling water for 20 minutes, liquid reserved

content.text: If using porcini, soak them in 100ml of boiling water for 20 minutes. Drain and roughly chop, keeping the liquid.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the rigatoni until 2 minutes short of the packet time. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.

Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide frying pan over a high heat. Add the chestnut mushrooms in a single layer. Cook without stirring for 3 minutes until deeply browned on one side, then stir and cook for 2 more minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and porcini. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it bubble until reduced by half.
If using porcini, add their soaking liquid now, pouring slowly and leaving any grit at the bottom of the bowl. Stir in the cream. Simmer for 3 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Add the drained rigatoni to the pan. Toss over the heat for 2 minutes, adding pasta water to loosen as needed.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the parmesan and season with black pepper. Scatter over parsley and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The mushrooms have no colour and are wet.
items.cause: The pan was overcrowded and the mushrooms steamed instead of frying.
items.fix: Cook in two batches over a high heat, leaving the mushrooms untouched for at least 3 minutes before stirring.

items.cause: The heat was too high after adding the cream.
items.fix: Keep the heat gentle once cream is in the pan; a simmer rather than a boil keeps the sauce smooth.

items.symptom: The pasta is too thick and stodgy.
items.fix: Keep the reserved pasta water close and add it a splash at a time while tossing until the sauce flows freely around the pasta.
